Feel like the sentiment on Jadarian Price is a bit too bearish after last night’s game.

He looked to be the clear best RB in this backfield already and was very efficient, despite the sluggish game environment.

He also earned a couple of targets and ran more routes than Holani.

The bigger issue for Price was losing out on short yardage work where Emanuel Wilson was subbing in, but we did see Price sub back in on that 2nd & 6 at the 8 yard line (at least not a complete aversion to using him near goal line).

It’s also still very early of course, and we see player roles’ change as the season progresses all the time (especially for rookies).

Seems premature to give up on Price scoring a bunch of TDs this year in a (likely) good offense based off usage in his 1st career game (a low-scoring game at that), and considering the lacking competition in this backfield at the moment.

There will be plenty of better game environments for this Seattle offense, and for Price to make a bigger impact/turn his explosiveness into big performances. I’m optimistic he can still be a big hit at his RB23 ADP in drafts.

Love backing Williams here. He’s coming off a breakout 2025 season where he topped 1,000+ receiving yards and averaged 65.7 yards per game on 102 targets.

The biggest thing that stands out is his big play ability. Williams averaged 17.2 yards per reception last season, which was among the best in the league. He doesn’t need a massive target volume to do damage because a couple of deep completions can put him over this number quickly.

This line is also sitting below his 2025 average, so if he’s anywhere near his usual efficiency, he only needs around 3-4 catches to get there. That’s a pretty favorable setup for a receiver who can rack up yards in chunks.

Williams also became much more involved as the season went on. From Weeks 10-18, he averaged 84.7 receiving yards per game while seeing an 18.5% target share. Compare that to just 44.4 yards per game and a 14.9% target share over Weeks 1-9.

At this number, I’m willing to bet on the talent and the big play upside. A receiver who averaged 65.7 yards per game last season and has legitimate 20-40+ yard play potential feels like he’s being priced a little too low here.

More than 10 yards:
Allen: 15
Lamar: 11

Allen STILL leads.

30-24.

Lamar’s 36th rushing TD came yesterday from the 5-yard line — with Derrick Henry in the backfield.

Allen’s 80th came yesterday from 21 yards out.

Remember when I pointed out how low Carson Wentz's air yards were in 2016 and started getting death threats from Eagles fans?

Now I see that stat used all the time here and not in a good way. Because it was always a playing STYLE stat rather than one where you want to get to the top of the list.

A stat where it's not really good to be at either end of the extreme, and I don't think most people are able to grasp that concept.

If your air yards are too high, you probably miss easy completions that keep the offense on schedule.

If your air yards are too low, you probably stagnate the offense by not taking enough chances.

And if you take a lot of sacks, aDOT doesn't even care about those plays. Good sack avoidance can actually hurt your aDOT if you're good at checking down and throwing the ball away.

It's a stat that requires more nuance than being thrown on the axis of a graph and treated as low is bad, high is good.

Matchup concerns aside, it’s hard to not also be worried about Kraft’s potential role/snap count in his 1st game coming off the injury. There’s been talks about a snap count, and there’s a very real world where he’s a step slower early in the year.

On top of this, Kraft does have a really tough matchup in this one. The Brian Flores-led Vikings defense was 2nd in the NFL in EPA/DB, and they're generally a really tough matchup for opposing offenses.

In terms of coverages, Kraft gets absolutely nuked against both two-high (MIN led NFL in 2 high %) and zone (MIN ran at 7th highest %). Against 2-high looks, he saw his TPRR dip 36% (0.22→0.14) and his YPRR 39% (2.57→1.56). Similar story for zone, where he sees dips north of 30% in both TPRR (down to 0.15) and YPRR (down to 1.75).

The Vikings were also tough against inline/slot aligned players last year (where Kraft ran over 80% of his routes), as they were top 10 in YPG allowed to both, and top 5 in EPA/DB. 

And when GB is pressured (MIN was 8th in pressure rate, Flores is known for getting pressure in creative ways), like with Watson, Kraft’s efficiency plummets. His TPRR dropped down to 0.15, and his YPRR got cut by more than 50% (2.57→1.20) per @FantasyPtsData.

Given all this and the injury, it feels like there’s a ton working against Kraft in Week 1. I like the under on 46.5 receiving yards, and avoiding in DFS formats.
